q22007.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under a danger sign, gives the distance between the sign and the point where the danger begins.

explain.short: A number alone (no arrows) under a danger sign tells you how far ahead the danger starts.
explain.rule: A white panel with only a number in m or km (no arrows) is a DISTANCE panel: it tells how far ahead the danger, the rule or the place shown by the sign begins.
explain.trap: 'distanza' (distance) is right here; with arrows the panel would give a length instead.

sceneParams.caption: The danger starts 320 m after the sign

q22008.en: The supplementary panel shown can be placed under signs to complete their meaning.

explain.short: That is exactly the job of every supplementary panel: it adds a detail (here a distance) to the sign above it.
explain.rule: Supplementary panels (pannelli integrativi) are small white plates under a sign. They complete or limit its meaning: distance, length, hours, days, vehicles. This one gives a distance.
explain.trap: 'completarne il significato' (complete its meaning): the panel adds information, it never makes a rule on its own.

sceneParams.caption: A panel completes the sign above it

q22009.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under an information sign, gives the distance still to go to reach the place shown by the sign.

explain.short: Under an information sign (e.g. a petrol station or a car park) the number tells you how far away that place is.
explain.rule: A white panel with only a number in m or km (no arrows) is a DISTANCE panel: it tells how far ahead the danger, the rule or the place shown by the sign begins.
explain.trap: 'distanza che manca' (distance still to go): it counts forward, not the road already done.

sceneParams.caption: The place on the sign is 320 m ahead

q22010.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under a mandatory or prohibition sign, gives the distance from which the rule starts.

explain.short: Under a ban or an order, the number tells you how far ahead the rule begins to apply.
explain.rule: A white panel with only a number in m or km (no arrows) is a DISTANCE panel: it tells how far ahead the danger, the rule or the place shown by the sign begins.
explain.trap: 'distanza dalla quale inizia' (distance from which it starts): it is a distance, not the length of the stretch.

keywords.en: the distance from which it starts

q22011.en: The supplementary panel shown in figure A shows the metres of road already travelled.

explain.short: The number looks forward: it is the distance to something ahead, not the road you have already done.
explain.rule: A white panel with only a number in m or km (no arrows) is a DISTANCE panel: it tells how far ahead the danger, the rule or the place shown by the sign begins.
explain.trap: 'già fatta' (already done) is the trick: the panel never counts road behind you.

sceneParams.caption: Distance AHEAD, not road already done

q22012.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates the gradient of a road.

explain.short: A gradient is written in percent (%) on the steep-hill sign. This panel shows metres or kilometres: a distance.
explain.rule: A white panel with only a number in m or km (no arrows) is a DISTANCE panel: it tells how far ahead the danger, the rule or the place shown by the sign begins.
explain.trap: 'pendenza' (gradient, slope) is the wrong idea: m and km are distances, a slope is in %.

sceneParams.caption: A distance in m/km, not a slope in %

q22013.en: The supplementary panel shown in figure A indicates the safety distance to keep from the vehicle in front.

explain.short: The panel tells where the danger or rule of the sign begins. It says nothing about the gap to the car ahead.
explain.rule: A white panel with only a number in m or km (no arrows) is a DISTANCE panel: it tells how far ahead the danger, the rule or the place shown by the sign begins.
explain.trap: 'distanza di sicurezza' (safety distance) sounds right because of 'distance', but it is a different idea.

sceneParams.caption: Distance to the danger, not a safety gap

q22014.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates the width of a road.

explain.short: The number is a distance along the road to the danger or rule. Road width is never shown on this panel.
explain.rule: A white panel with only a number in m or km (no arrows) is a DISTANCE panel: it tells how far ahead the danger, the rule or the place shown by the sign begins.
explain.trap: 'larghezza' (width) is invented: the panel measures how far ahead, not how wide.

q22015.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under the danger sign, indicates the length of the dangerous stretch of road.

explain.short: Without arrows the number is a distance (where the danger starts). The length is shown by the panel with up arrows on both sides.
explain.rule: A white panel with only a number in m or km (no arrows) is a DISTANCE panel: it tells how far ahead the danger, the rule or the place shown by the sign begins.
explain.trap: 'lunghezza' (length) is the trap: no arrows = distance, arrows = length.

sceneParams.caption: No arrows: distance to the start, not length

q22016.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under a danger sign, indicates the length of the dangerous stretch of road.

explain.short: The two up arrows mean 'for this long': the danger lasts for the stretch written on the panel.
explain.rule: A white panel with a number between two up arrows is an EXTENSION panel: it tells how LONG the stretch is where the danger or the rule of the sign lasts.
explain.trap: 'lunghezza' (length) is right here because of the arrows; without arrows it would be a distance.

q22017.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under a mandatory sign, indicates the length of the stretch of road where the sign's rule applies.

explain.short: Under an order sign, the arrows panel tells for how many metres the order lasts.
explain.rule: A white panel with a number between two up arrows is an EXTENSION panel: it tells how LONG the stretch is where the danger or the rule of the sign lasts.
explain.trap: 'lunghezza del tratto' (length of the stretch) matches the arrows: it is not where the rule starts.

keywords.en: the length of the stretch of road

q22018.en: The supplementary panel shown can be placed under a prohibition sign.

explain.short: Yes: under a ban (for example no overtaking) it tells how long the ban lasts.
explain.rule: A white panel with a number between two up arrows is an EXTENSION panel: it tells how LONG the stretch is where the danger or the rule of the sign lasts.
explain.trap: 'può' (can): the panel can go under danger, mandatory AND prohibition signs.

sceneParams.caption: Under a ban: the ban lasts for 380 m

q22019.en: The supplementary panel shown in figure B, placed under a danger sign, indicates, in kilometres, the length of the dangerous stretch of road.

explain.short: Panel B has arrows and '2,8 km': the danger lasts for 2.8 kilometres.
explain.rule: A white panel with a number between two up arrows is an EXTENSION panel: it tells how LONG the stretch is where the danger or the rule of the sign lasts.
explain.trap: 'in chilometri' (in kilometres): panel B says km, panel A says m; both with arrows are lengths.

q22020.en: The sign shown indicates the length of a stretch of road with dangerous bends one after the other.

explain.short: The triangle warns of a series of dangerous bends; the arrows panel says they go on for 380 m.
explain.rule: A white panel with a number between two up arrows is an EXTENSION panel: it tells how LONG the stretch is where the danger or the rule of the sign lasts.
explain.trap: 'lunghezza' (length) is right because the panel has arrows; 'in successione' (one after the other) matches the double bend.

q22021.en: The supplementary panel shown in figure A requires you to go straight on for 380 metres.

explain.short: The arrows do not mean 'go straight': they only show that the sign above is valid for the next 380 m.
explain.rule: A white panel with a number between two up arrows is an EXTENSION panel: it tells how LONG the stretch is where the danger or the rule of the sign lasts.
explain.trap: 'obbliga' (requires): a panel never creates an order by itself; the arrows show length, not direction.

keywords.en: requires you to go straight on

q22022.en: The supplementary panel shown in figure A indicates the safety distance to keep when it rains.

explain.short: The panel tells how long the stretch of the sign above is. It has nothing to do with rain or safety distance.
explain.rule: A white panel with a number between two up arrows is an EXTENSION panel: it tells how LONG the stretch is where the danger or the rule of the sign lasts.
explain.trap: 'distanza di sicurezza in caso di pioggia' is invented: the panel shows a length, not a following gap.

sceneParams.caption: Length of the stretch, not a rain gap

q22023.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates the distance between the sign and the point where the danger begins.

explain.short: With arrows on both sides the number is the LENGTH of the dangerous stretch. The distance panel has no arrows.
explain.rule: A white panel with a number between two up arrows is an EXTENSION panel: it tells how LONG the stretch is where the danger or the rule of the sign lasts.
explain.trap: 'distanza' (distance) is the trap: arrows = length, no arrows = distance.

sceneParams.caption: Arrows: length of the danger, not distance

q22024.en: The sign shown indicates the distance between the sign and the start of the road in bad condition.

explain.short: The triangle warns of an uneven road; the arrows panel says the bad road lasts for 380 m. It starts right at the sign.
explain.rule: A white panel with a number between two up arrows is an EXTENSION panel: it tells how LONG the stretch is where the danger or the rule of the sign lasts.
explain.trap: 'distanza' (distance) is wrong: with arrows the 380 m is the length of the bad stretch.

sceneParams.caption: Uneven road FOR 380 m, starting here

q22025.en: The supplementary panel shown in figure A indicates the height of a viaduct.

explain.short: The panel gives the length of a stretch of road, not the height of anything.
explain.rule: A white panel with a number between two up arrows is an EXTENSION panel: it tells how LONG the stretch is where the danger or the rule of the sign lasts.
explain.trap: 'altezza' (height) is invented: a height limit has its own round sign in metres.

sceneParams.caption: Length of a stretch, not a height

q22026.en: The sign shown forbids parking from 7.30 to 19.00.

explain.short: No-parking sign plus an hours panel: parking is banned only between 7.30 and 19.00.
explain.rule: A white panel with only hours (e.g. 7.30-19.00) limits the sign above it to those hours, every day. Outside those hours the sign does not apply.
explain.trap: 'dalle ore 7.30 alle ore 19.00' matches the panel; outside those hours parking is allowed.

q22027.en: The sign shown forbids transit from 7.30 to 19.00.

explain.short: The plain red ring is 'no vehicles'; the panel limits the ban to 7.30-19.00.
explain.rule: A white panel with only hours (e.g. 7.30-19.00) limits the sign above it to those hours, every day. Outside those hours the sign does not apply.
explain.trap: 'vieta il transito' is right: the panel does not change the ban, it only sets its hours.

q22028.en: The supplementary panel (A), placed under the sign (B), forbids pedestrians to pass only in the hours shown.

explain.short: Sign B bans pedestrians; panel A limits that ban to 7.30-19.00. Outside those hours pedestrians may pass.
explain.rule: A white panel with only hours (e.g. 7.30-19.00) limits the sign above it to those hours, every day. Outside those hours the sign does not apply.
explain.trap: 'nelle sole ore indicate' (only in the hours shown) is the panel's job: it limits the sign above.

q22029.en: The supplementary panel shown in figure B indicates the hours of every day in which the sign applies.

explain.short: Panel B shows only hours, with no day symbol, so the sign applies every day in those hours.
explain.rule: An hours-only panel limits the sign above it to those hours, every day. Panel A '0-24' means the sign applies all day and night.
explain.trap: 'tutti i giorni' (every day) is right: no cross and no hammers means no day limit.

keywords.it: le ore di tutti i giorni

q22030.en: The sign shown allows motorcycles to pass only in the hours shown.

explain.short: The sign BANS motorcycles; the panel says the ban applies 7.30-19.00. So motorcycles may pass only OUTSIDE those hours.
explain.rule: A white panel with only hours (e.g. 7.30-19.00) limits the sign above it to those hours, every day. Outside those hours the sign does not apply.
explain.trap: 'consente' (allows) flips the meaning: in the hours shown motorcycles are forbidden.

q22031.en: The sign shown indicates that the horn may be used from 7.30 to 19.00.

explain.short: The crossed-out horn means 'no horn'; the panel says the ban applies from 7.30 to 19.00.
explain.rule: An hours panel limits the sign above it to those hours. Here the crossed-out horn (no horn) applies only from 7.30 to 19.00.
explain.trap: 'può essere usato' (may be used) is the opposite: in those hours the horn is forbidden.

q22032.en: The sign shown indicates the opening hours of a limited traffic zone.

explain.short: The blue sign with a pedestrian is a pedestrian path; the panel (cross = holidays) says it is for pedestrians only on holidays, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel only limits the sign above it. Here the pedestrian-path sign applies on holidays (cross) from 8.00 to 20.00.
explain.trap: 'zona a traffico limitato' (restricted traffic zone, ZTL) has its own sign; this is a pedestrian path with a time limit.

sceneParams.caption: Pedestrian path on holidays 8-20, not a ZTL

q22033.en: The supplementary panel shown in figure B indicates the hours in which you may drive with your lights off.

explain.short: Panel B only gives the hours in which the sign above applies. It has nothing to do with headlights.
explain.rule: A white panel with only hours (e.g. 7.30-19.00) limits the sign above it to those hours, every day. Outside those hours the sign does not apply.
explain.trap: 'fari spenti' (lights off) is invented: a panel never creates a rule on its own.

sceneParams.caption: Hours of the sign, not 'lights off'

q22034.en: The supplementary panel shown in figure B indicates the time slots in which odd/even number plate driving applies.

explain.short: Panel B only gives the hours in which the sign above applies. Alternate number plates are a separate local order.
explain.rule: A white panel with only hours (e.g. 7.30-19.00) limits the sign above it to those hours, every day. Outside those hours the sign does not apply.
explain.trap: 'targhe alterne' (odd/even plates) is invented: the panel only sets the hours of its sign.

sceneParams.caption: Hours of the sign, not odd/even plates

q22035.en: The supplementary panel shown limits the validity of the sign it is under to holidays and to the time slot shown.

explain.short: The small cross means holidays: the sign above applies only on holidays, from 8.00 to 20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'limita la validità' (limits the validity) is exactly what a panel does.

q22036.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under a regulatory sign, states that the sign applies only on holidays and in the time slots shown.

explain.short: Under a ban or an order, the cross panel limits it to holidays and to the hours written.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'solo nei giorni festivi' (only on holidays) is right: on working days the sign does not apply.

q22037.en: The sign shown allows only pedestrians to pass on holidays in the time slots shown.

explain.short: The blue pedestrian sign is a pedestrian path: only pedestrians may use it. The cross panel limits this to holidays, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'ai soli pedoni' (only pedestrians) is right for the pedestrian path; the panel only adds when.

q22038.en: The sign shown forbids parking in the time slot shown, on holidays.

explain.short: No-parking sign plus cross panel: no parking on holidays from 8.00 to 20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'dei giorni festivi' (on holidays) matches the cross; on working days parking is not banned by this sign.

q22039.en: The sign shown allows only cyclists to pass from 8.00 to 20.00 on holidays.

explain.short: The blue bicycle sign is a cycle path: only bicycles may use it. The cross panel limits this to holidays, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'ai soli ciclisti' (only cyclists) is right; the panel says it applies on holidays in those hours.

q22040.en: The sign shown forbids transit from 8.00 to 20.00 on holidays.

explain.short: No-vehicles sign plus cross panel: no vehicles on holidays from 8.00 to 20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'dei giorni festivi' (on holidays) matches the small cross on the panel.

q22041.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates the entry hours of the cemetery.

explain.short: The cross is the symbol for holidays, not a cemetery. The panel limits the sign above it to holidays, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'cimitero' (cemetery) plays on the cross: it means holidays (giorni festivi).

q22042.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates the opening hours of churches.

explain.short: The cross is the symbol for holidays, not a church. The panel limits the sign above it to holidays, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'chiese' (churches) plays on the cross: it means holidays (giorni festivi).

q22043.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates the times of religious services.

explain.short: The cross is the symbol for holidays. The panel only says when the sign above applies: holidays, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'funzioni religiose' (religious services) plays on the cross: it means holidays (giorni festivi).

q22044.en: The sign shown indicates that you may park every day in the time slot shown.

explain.short: The car park is valid only on holidays (cross), from 8.00 to 20.00, not every day.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'tutti i giorni' (every day) is wrong: the cross limits it to holidays.

q22045.en: The supplementary panel shown applies on working days.

explain.short: The cross means holidays. Working days are shown by a different symbol: two crossed hammers.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'giorni lavorativi' (working days) is the opposite: cross = holidays, hammers = working days.

q22046.en: The sign shown allows motorcycles to pass on Sundays from 8.00 to 20.00.

explain.short: The sign BANS motorcycles; the cross panel says the ban applies on holidays (Sundays too) from 8.00 to 20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with a small cross and hours means HOLIDAYS (giorni festivi, Sundays and public holidays): the sign above applies only on holidays, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'consente' (allows) flips the meaning: in that time motorcycles are forbidden.

q22047.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under a sign, limits its validity to working days and to the time slots shown.

explain.short: The crossed hammers mean working days: the sign above applies only on working days, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'giorni lavorativi' (working days) matches the hammers; a cross would mean holidays.

q22048.en: The sign shown forbids transit in the time slot shown, on working days.

explain.short: No-vehicles sign plus hammers panel: no vehicles on working days from 8.00 to 20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'dei giorni lavorativi' (on working days) matches the hammers.

q22049.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates the time slot on working days during which the rule of the sign it is under applies.

explain.short: Hammers mean working days; the hours say when, on those days, the sign above applies.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'giorni lavorativi' (working days) is right for the hammers symbol.

q22050.en: The sign shown forbids parking in the time slot shown on working days.

explain.short: No-parking sign plus hammers panel: no parking on working days from 8.00 to 20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'dei giorni lavorativi' (on working days) matches the hammers; on holidays this sign does not apply.

q22051.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under a mandatory sign, indicates that it applies from 8.00 to 20.00 on working days.

explain.short: Under an order sign, the hammers panel limits the order to working days, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'dei giorni lavorativi' (on working days) matches the hammers; the panel works under orders too.

sceneParams.caption: The order applies on working days, 8-20

q22052.en: The sign shown forbids transit to lorries with a total mass over 3.5 t in the hours shown, on working days.

explain.short: The red ring with a lorry bans lorries over 3.5 t; the hammers panel limits the ban to working days, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'dei giorni lavorativi' (on working days) matches the hammers; on holidays these lorries may pass.

sceneParams.caption: Lorries over 3.5 t banned, working days 8-20

q22053.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates that the sign it is paired with applies every day, but only in the hours shown.

explain.short: The crossed hammers limit the sign to working days only, not every day.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'tutti i giorni' (every day) is wrong: the hammers mean working days only.

sceneParams.caption: Working days only, not every day

q22054.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates the opening hours of a museum of work tools.

explain.short: The hammers are the symbol for working days, not tools in a museum. The panel limits the sign above it.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'museo di attrezzi da lavoro' plays on the hammers: they mean working days (giorni lavorativi).

sceneParams.caption: Hammers = working days, not a museum

q22055.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates the opening hours of roadside recovery workshops.

explain.short: The hammers are the symbol for working days, not a workshop. The panel limits the sign above it to working days, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'officine di soccorso stradale' plays on the hammers: they mean working days (giorni lavorativi).

sceneParams.caption: Hammers = working days, not a workshop

q22056.en: The sign shown is reserved for roadside recovery vehicles.

explain.short: It is a normal car park for everyone; the hammers panel only limits it to working days, 8.00-20.00.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'soccorso stradale' (roadside recovery) plays on the hammers: they mean working days.

sceneParams.caption: Car park on working days 8-20, for all

q22057.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates that the sign it is paired with applies on holidays.

explain.short: The crossed hammers mean working days. Holidays are shown by a small cross instead.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'giorni festivi' (holidays) is the opposite: hammers = working days, cross = holidays.

q22058.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under the PARKING sign, indicates that you may park on holidays from 8.00 to 20.00.

explain.short: Under a parking sign, the hammers panel means the car park is valid on working days 8.00-20.00, not on holidays.
explain.rule: A panel with crossed hammers and hours means WORKING DAYS (giorni lavorativi, Monday to Saturday except holidays): the sign above applies only on working days, in those hours.
explain.trap: 'giorni festivi' (holidays) is wrong: the hammers mean working days.

sceneParams.caption: Parking on working days, not holidays

q22059.en: The sign shown forbids transit only to the vehicles shown.

explain.short: The no-vehicles sign is limited by the panel to articulated lorries: only they are banned.
explain.rule: A panel with a vehicle drawing limits the sign above it to that kind of vehicle only. Here it is an articulated lorry (autoarticolato: tractor unit + semi-trailer).
explain.trap: 'ai soli veicoli indicati' (only to the vehicles shown) is right: the panel narrows the ban.

q22060.en: The sign shown forbids parking to the vehicles shown.

explain.short: The sign is 'no stopping' (red X), limited to articulated lorries. No stopping also means no parking for them.
explain.rule: A vehicle panel limits the sign above it to those vehicles. Here 'no stopping' (divieto di fermata) applies only to articulated lorries; it includes no parking.
explain.trap: 'vieta la sosta' (forbids parking) is right even though the sign bans stopping: no stopping includes no parking.

sceneParams.caption: No stopping (so no parking) for these lorries

q22061.en: The sign shown forbids articulated lorries to park.

explain.short: No-parking sign plus a panel with an articulated lorry: the parking ban is only for those vehicles.
explain.rule: A panel with a vehicle drawing limits the sign above it to that kind of vehicle only. Here it is an articulated lorry (autoarticolato: tractor unit + semi-trailer).
explain.trap: 'agli autoarticolati' (to articulated lorries) is right: that is the vehicle drawn on the panel.

q22062.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates that the sign it is paired with applies only to the vehicles shown.

explain.short: A vehicle panel narrows the sign above it: the rule is only for the vehicle drawn.
explain.rule: A panel with a vehicle drawing limits the sign above it to that kind of vehicle only. Here it is an articulated lorry (autoarticolato: tractor unit + semi-trailer).
explain.trap: 'solo per i veicoli rappresentati' (only for the vehicles shown) is exactly the job of this panel.

sceneParams.caption: The sign applies only to these vehicles

q22063.en: The supplementary panel shown can be paired with a mandatory sign.

explain.short: Yes: a vehicle panel can go under an order sign, so the order applies only to those vehicles.
explain.rule: A panel with a vehicle drawing limits the sign above it to that kind of vehicle only. Here it is an articulated lorry (autoarticolato: tractor unit + semi-trailer).
explain.trap: 'può' (can): vehicle panels go under orders and bans alike.

sceneParams.caption: Under an order: only for these vehicles

q22064.en: The supplementary panel shown can be paired with a prohibition sign.

explain.short: Yes: under a ban (for example no parking or no vehicles) it limits the ban to those vehicles.
explain.rule: A panel with a vehicle drawing limits the sign above it to that kind of vehicle only. Here it is an articulated lorry (autoarticolato: tractor unit + semi-trailer).
explain.trap: 'può' (can): vehicle panels go under bans and orders alike.

sceneParams.caption: Under a ban: only for these vehicles

q22065.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates a mechanic's workshop for lorries with trailers.

explain.short: The panel is not a service sign: it only says which vehicles the sign above applies to.
explain.rule: A panel with a vehicle drawing limits the sign above it to that kind of vehicle only. Here it is an articulated lorry (autoarticolato: tractor unit + semi-trailer).
explain.trap: 'officina meccanica' (workshop) is invented: the panel only names the vehicles.

q22066.en: The supplementary panel shown indicates a filling station for heavy vehicles only.

explain.short: The panel is not a service sign: it only says which vehicles the sign above applies to.
explain.rule: A panel with a vehicle drawing limits the sign above it to that kind of vehicle only. Here it is an articulated lorry (autoarticolato: tractor unit + semi-trailer).
explain.trap: 'stazione di rifornimento' (filling station) is invented: the panel only names the vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Names vehicles, not a filling station

q22067.en: The sign shown allows articulated lorries to park.

explain.short: It is a no-parking sign: the panel says the BAN is for articulated lorries. They may not park.
explain.rule: A panel with a vehicle drawing limits the sign above it to that kind of vehicle only. Here it is an articulated lorry (autoarticolato: tractor unit + semi-trailer).
explain.trap: 'consente' (allows) flips the meaning: the panel limits a ban, it does not grant permission.

q22068.en: The sign shown says that articulated lorries may pass.

explain.short: It is a no-vehicles sign limited to articulated lorries: they are the ones that may NOT pass.
explain.rule: A panel with a vehicle drawing limits the sign above it to that kind of vehicle only. Here it is an articulated lorry (autoarticolato: tractor unit + semi-trailer).
explain.trap: 'possono transitare' (may pass) is the opposite: the vehicles on the panel are banned.

q22069.en: The supplementary panel shown, placed under the PARKING sign, indicates that all heavy vehicles may park.

explain.short: Under a parking sign the panel reserves the car park for the vehicle drawn: articulated lorries only, not all heavy vehicles.
explain.rule: A panel with a vehicle drawing limits the sign above it to that kind of vehicle only. Here it is an articulated lorry (autoarticolato: tractor unit + semi-trailer).
explain.trap: 'tutti i veicoli pesanti' (all heavy vehicles) is too wide: only the vehicle drawn counts.
